rules: Anki first thing, every day. Micro sections I and II live there now.
The bacteriology background track runs EVERY day from 6 Nov. It is small on purpose. It is the one thing that is never skipped — section V of the final is unanswerable without it.

Tripwire: by 26 Nov you should have ~40 topics of section I/II done. Under 30 means drop the pharm semifinal to January and keep the micro final in December. Decide by the count, not by how you feel that week.
On a bad day shed pathophysiology first, then pharmacology, then patho slides. Never shed the next exam's subject and never shed the bacteriology track.
Nothing new after swim training. Tuesday and Thursday evenings are review only.
Wednesday is the shortest day — ECG practical 17:30–19:00 plus 80 minutes of commuting. Never move work into it; move work to Saturday.
A missed day pushes everything back one slot. Do not double up.
Pharm A1–A9 is deliberately after MT2 rather than before it. A10–A22 is what the 16 Nov exam asks; A1–A9 is revision for the semifinal.
MT2 is DNA viruses only — III 1–19. RNA viruses (III 20–37) are final-exam scope and are covered in the December block via section V and blurting.

Genetics + immunology is a question bank of 2000–3000 items. Grind the bank first and use Abbas and the lectures only to patch what the bank exposes. It needs 50% in BOTH halves, so neither genetics nor immunology can be left thin.
Every winter date is yours to choose. Micro and pharm sit pre-Christmas because both peak then and a December failure still has January to retake. Pathophys and genetics/immunology are January.
The Christmas break is a buffer, not a plan. If December goes well it becomes the start of genetics and immunology.

tasks.detail: Short night — 06:15 practice tomorrow.
